title: i0jtaq
The Event of Mubahala and the Trust of the Ahl al-Bayt
hook: The Prophet brought out the Ahl al-Bayt for the mubahala. He left the Book and the itra (his kin) as a trust, so that they would not be separated.
scenes.0.text: A delegation came to Medina from Najran. They were Christians. The discussion centered on Jesus. They spoke of Jesus as the son of God and as a deity. The Prophet said that Jesus was a servant of God. The talk dragged on. Both sides held to their own word. Then the verse of mubahala was revealed. Mubahala is when both sides turn to God and call down a curse on the side that lies. Âl-i İmrân 61 says: let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us invoke God's curse upon the liars. In the morning the Prophet came out of his house. With him was **Imam Ali**, who was like his own self, that is, whom he placed in the position of himself. His daughter **Lady Fatima** was with him. His grandsons **Imam Hasan** and **Imam Husayn** were with him. He called no one else. He said, "O God, these are my family." When the Christians of Najran saw this procession, they stopped. No army had come out before them. The people the Prophet loved most had come out. They did not dare to exchange curses. They accepted the agreement. That day, the Ahl al-Bayt stood on that field.

scenes.1.text: The word "ourselves" in the verse of mubahala includes **Imam Ali**. The Prophet brought him to the mubahala as his own self. This closeness was not merely kinship. The Prophet had placed **Imam Ali** in the place where he himself stood. Wilaya, that is, leadership, is the name of this place.

scenes.2.text: On the return from the Farewell Pilgrimage, the caravan reached the waters of Khumm. There the Prophet left two weighty trusts: the Book of God and his itra, that is, ==the Ahl al-Bayt==. He said, "I remind you of God regarding my Ahl al-Bayt." These two will not be separated until they reach the Hawd. The Hawd is the pool on the Day of Resurrection. When Zayd was asked, he kept the wives outside the close circle. He named the families of Ali, Aqil, Ja'far and Abbas. The Prophet bound the Book and the itra together so that the Qur'an would not be left without the Ahl al-Bayt.

scenes.3.text: The Prophet also said this about the Ahl al-Bayt: "The example of my Ahl al-Bayt is like the Ark of Noah. Whoever boards it is saved; the rest drown." This saying is called Safina. Safina means ship. The ship pointed out at Ghadir was the Ahl al-Bayt. When people abandoned them at Saqifa, the Ummah fell into a heavy distress.
scenes.4.text: Jabir b. Samura narrates. The Prophet said, "This matter will continue until twelve caliphs have come from among them." Then he said something more. Jabir could not hear it. His father reported that the Prophet said, "All of them are from Quraysh." This number is not arbitrary. Imamate, that is, the leadership of the imams, is a line of twelve persons.

scenes.5.text: These twelve are the Twelve Imams appointed by God. According to the narration, Jabir saw a tablet in the hand of **Lady Fatima**. The names of the imams were written on it. The number stood on this tablet, name by name.

scenes.6.text: ==Imamate== is leadership designated by God through nass. Nass means an explicit declaration. The imam is protected from sin and is superior in knowledge. The earth is never without a hujja. The hujja is the imam whom God has made a proof. Each imam announces the one after him. Ghadir had shown the first person of this line to everyone.

scenes.7.text: The Twelve Imams are these: **Imam Ali**, **Imam Hasan**, **Imam Husayn**, Imam Zayn al-Abidin, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, Imam Musa al-Kazim, Imam Ali al-Rida, Imam Muhammad al-Taqi, Imam Ali al-Naqi, Imam Hasan al-Askari and **Imam Mahdi**. The twelfth imam is in occultation. This is called ghayba. When the time comes, he will emerge with justice. **Imam Husayn** was martyred at Karbala. This line of the Twelve Imams is completed with **Imam Mahdi**.

sunni.0.says: When the verse of mubahala was revealed, the Prophet called Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn and said, "O God, these are my family."
sunni.1.says: Two weighty trusts at the waters of Khumm: the Book of God and the Ahl al-Bayt; debate over its scope.
sunni.2.says: The Book and the itra will not be separated until they reach the Prophet at the Hawd.
sunni.3.says: The Ahl al-Bayt are like the Ark of Noah; al-Hakim gives a ruling of authenticity. Al-Dhahabi's ruling in the Talkhis could not be verified in this session.
sunni.3.grade: Al-Hakim: sahih; some hadith scholars consider it weak (disputed)
sunni.4.says: Jabir b. Samura: "There will be twelve amirs"; his father says, "All of them are from Quraysh."
sunni.5.says: Jabir b. Samura: "This caliphate will continue until twelve caliphs have come"; all of them are from Quraysh.
shia.0.says: Imamate is by nass, the hujja will never be lacking, and the narration of the tablet that Jabir saw with Lady Fatima.
shia.1.says: Narrations giving the names of the twelve imams, and the occultation.
shia.2.says: Narrations from the Prophet about twelve caliphs/imams; the occultation of the twelfth imam.
shia.3.says: The chains of the Safina hadith in Shia and Sunni sources, and al-Hakim's ruling of authenticity.
shia.4.says: The transmission of the tablet hadith in al-Kafi, Kamal al-Din and al-Nu'mani's al-Ghayba; al-Barqi's criticism.
disputes.0.title: mog26s
Who is "ourselves" in the mubahala?
disputes.0.sunni: The Prophet brought out Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn to the mubahala; this is a great merit. In the Sunni reading, the verse gives no ruling about the caliphate.
disputes.0.shia: The Prophet brought out Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn to the mubahala; this is a great merit. In Shia thought, the word "anfusana" (ourselves) makes Ali the self of the Prophet and shows his unique position.
disputes.1.title: 11lfo4i
Thaqalayn: "my itra" or "my sunna"?
disputes.1.sunni: In Muslim and Tirmidhi, the Prophet leaves the trust of "the Book and the itra." In the Sunni reading, the wording "the Book and my sunna" is also narrated; the saying means love and respect for the Ahl al-Bayt and is not counted as proof of imamate.
disputes.1.shia: In Muslim and Tirmidhi, the Prophet leaves the trust of "the Book and the itra." In Shia thought, this wording is authentic; that they are not separated from the Qur'an shows that the Ahl al-Bayt are the measure in religion.
disputes.2.title: kqg6ik
The authenticity of the Safina hadith
disputes.2.sunni: Al-Hakim relates the Safina hadith from Abu Dharr in al-Mustadrak. Although al-Hakim calls it sahih, some hadith scholars find its chains weak.
disputes.2.shia: Al-Hakim relates the Safina hadith from Abu Dharr in al-Mustadrak. In Shia thought, because it has come through many routes, it is regarded as certain in meaning.
disputes.3.title: qzqwdl
Who are the "twelve caliphs"?
disputes.3.sunni: Bukhari and Muslim mention twelve amirs or twelve caliphs; all are from Quraysh and the hadith names no one. In the Sunni reading, this number is explained by the first caliphs, the Umayyad caliphs, or future just rulers; a matching of names with the twelve imams does not exist in these sources.
disputes.3.shia: Bukhari and Muslim mention twelve amirs or twelve caliphs; all are from Quraysh and the hadith names no one. In Shia thought, the number corresponds to the Twelve Imams; al-Kafi, al-Ghayba and Kamal al-Din report the names, while some Shia scholars such as al-Barqi have criticized the tablet narration in terms of text and chain.
questions.0: The Prophet came before the Najran delegation with Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn. How does this choice grow love for the Ahl al-Bayt within you?
questions.1: The Prophet left the Ahl al-Bayt as a trust together with the Book. How can you make room for this trust in your daily life?
questions.2: The number "twelve" stands in Bukhari and Muslim. The Shia match this number with the names of the Twelve Imams. How does learning these names make you feel?
questions.3: The Safina hadith likens the Ahl al-Bayt to Noah's Ark. Even though its chain is debated, does this comparison make you think about what holding fast to them tells you?
summary: The sayings on the mubahala, the two trusts and the twelve caliphs show the place of the Ahl al-Bayt. These also appear in Sunni sources (Muslim, Sahih; Tirmidhi, al-Jami', no. 3788; Bukhari, Sahih, no. 7222; Muslim, Sahih, no. 1821). The Shia take them as evidence for the divine appointment of Ali and the Twelve Imams descended from him.
key: Mubahala: the Prophet brought only the Ahl al-Bayt with him
notes.0: The mubahala is a call to mutual cursing made with the Christian delegation of Najran (Âl-i İmrân 3:61).
notes.1: The Prophet brought Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn with him.
notes.2: The people of Najran shrank from mutual cursing and accepted the agreement.
notes.3: The Prophet said, on the return from the Farewell Pilgrimage, that he was leaving the Book and the Ahl al-Bayt as a trust (Muslim 2408, Tirmidhi 3788).
notes.4: The "twelve caliphs" hadith is read as referring to the imams of the Ahl al-Bayt.
